frames.label: In Blender, modifiers enable non-destructive modeling by applying effects like subdivision automatically without alte...
frames.main_point: In Blender, modifiers enable non-destructive modeling by applying effects like subdivision automatically without altering the base mesh geometry. This allows complex changes to be updated without manual rework.
frames.source_quote: Modifiers are automatic operations that affect an object in a non-destructive way. With modifiers, you can perform many effects automatically that would otherwise be too tedious to update manually (such as subdivision surfaces) and without affecting the base geometry of your object.
frames.subject: Blender modifiers (non-destructive editing)
frames.thread_title: CAD: How to model complicated smooth shapes?

frames.label: Blender modifiers affect only the display/rendered result, leaving the underlying editable geometry untouched
frames.main_point: Blender modifiers affect only the display/rendered result, leaving the underlying editable geometry untouched. You continue to edit the base mesh while the modifier alters the visual outcome.
frames.source_quote: They work by changing how an object is displayed and rendered, but not the geometry which you can edit directly.
frames.subject: Modifier effect vs editable geometry
frames.thread_title: CAD: How to model complicated smooth shapes?

frames.label: Multiple modifiers can be stacked on one object, and applying a modifier bakes its effect into permanent geometry
frames.main_point: Multiple modifiers can be stacked on one object, and applying a modifier bakes its effect into permanent geometry. This lets you layer operations and decide when to commit results.
frames.source_quote: You can add several modifiers to a single object to form The Modifier Stack and Apply a modifier if you wish to make its changes permanent.
frames.subject: Modifier stack and applying modifiers
frames.thread_title: CAD: How to model complicated smooth shapes?

frames.label: The Modify category targets auxiliary data (e.g., vertex groups) rather than altering the mesh geometry itself
frames.main_point: The Modify category targets auxiliary data (e.g., vertex groups) rather than altering the mesh geometry itself. It behaves similarly to Deform tools but operates on non-geometry data.
frames.source_quote: These are tools similar to the Deform ones (see below), however, they usually do not directly affect the geometry of the object, but some other data, such as vertex groups.
frames.subject: Modify category affects data, not geometry
frames.thread_title: CAD: How to model complicated smooth shapes?

frames.label: Generate modifiers operate on the entire mesh topology, changing overall form and potentially creating new geometry
frames.main_point: Generate modifiers operate on the entire mesh topology, changing overall form and potentially creating new geometry. They are constructive/destructive operations at the mesh level.
frames.source_quote: These are constructive/destructive tools that will affect the whole Topology of the mesh. They can change the general appearance of the object, or add new geometry to it
frames.subject: Generate modifiers affect topology and add geometry
frames.thread_title: CAD: How to model complicated smooth shapes?

frames.label: Deform modifiers modify an object's shape while preserving its topology
frames.main_point: Deform modifiers modify an object's shape while preserving its topology. They do not add or remove geometry.
frames.source_quote: Unlike Generate ones above, these only change the shape of an object, without altering its topology.
frames.subject: Deform modifiers preserve topology
frames.thread_title: CAD: How to model complicated smooth shapes?

frames.label: Simulate modifiers correspond to physics simulations and are usually auto-inserted into the modifier stack when a par...
frames.main_point: Simulate modifiers correspond to physics simulations and are usually auto-inserted into the modifier stack when a particle system or physics sim is enabled.
frames.source_quote: Those represent physics simulations. In most cases, they are automatically added to the modifiers stack whenever a Particle System or Physics simulation is enabled.
frames.subject: Simulate modifiers auto-added with physics
frames.thread_title: CAD: How to model complicated smooth shapes?

frames.label: Simulate modifiers’ only role is to define the position in the modifier stack from which the simulation’s base data i...
frames.main_point: Simulate modifiers’ only role is to define the position in the modifier stack from which the simulation’s base data is taken; they typically have no attributes and are controlled by settings in separate sections of the Properties.
frames.source_quote: Their only role is to define the position in the modifier stack from which is taken the base data for the simulation they represent. As such, they typically have no attributes, and are controlled by settings exposed in separate sections of the Properties.
frames.subject: Simulate modifiers define stack position and have no attributes
frames.thread_title: CAD: How to model complicated smooth shapes?

frames.label: In Blender, the currently active modifier determines which node group the Geometry Node Editor edits
frames.main_point: In Blender, the currently active modifier determines which node group the Geometry Node Editor edits. Choosing the active modifier sets the node group context.
frames.source_quote: The active modifier is used by the Geometry Node Editor to determine which node group is being modified.
frames.subject: Active modifier selection and Geometry Node Editor
